heroHeadline: Day 598: Sheinbaum Signs Historic EU-Mexico Trade Deal with Costa and Von der Leyen — First Summit in 11 Years
heroSubtitle: On May 22, 2026 (Day 598), President Claudia Sheinbaum hosted the 8th EU-Mexico Summit at the National Palace — the first EU-Mexico leader-level meeting in 11 years. EU Council President António Costa and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen signed two landmark agreements: the Modernised Global Agreement (replacing the 2000 EU-Mexico framework) and the Interim Trade Agreement (immediately effective). All 27 EU member states unanimously endorsed the deal on May 11. Key provisions: eliminates 95% of high Mexican tariffs on EU agricultural products; protects 568 European Geographical Indications; introduces an Investment Court System; binding labor and environmental standards with independent enforcement; bans export restrictions on critical minerals (Mexico supplies 33% of EU's fluorspar). Projected 35-40% bilateral trade volume increase; combined market of 582 million people and $25.1 trillion GDP. Costa: 'a new chapter in our partnership.' The deal directly strengthens Mexico's USMCA negotiating hand three days before the first formal bilateral round (week of May 25). At her May 22 mañanera, Sheinbaum also endorsed Senate President Monreal's proposal to legally annul electoral victories where foreign interference is confirmed — 'In Mexico, Mexicans decide' — and confirmed ongoing dialogue on missing persons and the Port of Loreto dispute. The diplomatic week culminates with U.S. envoy visits set for ~May 27 and the first formal USMCA negotiating round the week of May 25.
